instructions: Rinse the rice in a sieve. Put it in a medium pot with 3 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Bring it to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice the zucchini into 1/4-inch rounds. Dice the tomatoes into 1/2-inch pieces and mince the garlic. In a bowl, whisk the tomato paste into the broth.

Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add half the zucchini in one layer with 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 3 minutes without moving it, then flip and cook for 2 minutes, until golden in spots. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil and cook the rest of the zucchini the same way, with 1/4 tsp of the salt. Return all the zucchini to the pan.
Add the garlic and the herbes de Provence and stir for 45 seconds, until the garlic smells fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the broth mixture. Bring it to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the zucchini is tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat. Tear in about 1/4 cup basil leaves and add the pepper. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Serve the zucchini and its sauce over the rice.
method_notes: The Family Friends Food courgette, garlic and tomato (4.2 from 10 ratings, so a fallback lead) is the lead: zucchini browned in olive oil, then garlic, tomatoes and a tomato paste and stock mix simmered into a sauce. The amounts are doubled for a main dish over rice. Herbes de Provence (from Love French Food's baked tian) and a finish of basil make it read Provencal. This is the stovetop dish rather than a baked tian, because the tian needs 40 minutes or more with onions softened first and its recipe uses Parmesan, which would break the vegan tag.
